# Pass 1 — kebra-nagast-ch69

Reviewer: adversarial pass 1. Read: conventions.md, runbook.md, the RUNBOOK reviewer paragraph, packet.md, units.json, known-forms.json, novel-forms.json, the published pilot (ch. 1), the ch. 68b review for style, and the earlier parts' units where a form recurs (ch. 27, 33–34, 36, 38–39, 49–52, 59, 60a/b). No modern translations; no internet; Dillmann unavailable, so every lexical call is hedged (?). `t` untouched: edits were made by script, which asserted every `t` unchanged; the joined `t` equals the packet Geʿez exactly (749 words); every unit ends at ። ፤ or ፨; `p: true` on the heading and on the one paragraph (units 0, 1), correct. No unit exceeds 28 words. Schema unchanged. Units are numbered from 0 (the heading is unit 0); the reader sees no unit numbers, so the notes' cross-references were turned into "above/below" where I touched them.

Overall: a careful draft that hedged its cruxes well. Faults: (a) two real grammar errors with sense consequences (ኢየኀድገክሙ taken as 1cs; ትረስ taken as ረሰየ instead of ወረሰ "inherit"); (b) a mislabelled imperative (ብቊዐኒ as a noun); (c) a rendering of ተሀየየ that ignores the published ch. 60 rendering; (d) the ለ-owner construction after an anticipating suffix misread in unit 15 (and ኅይስና at odds with ch. 27 / 33–34); (e) `l` ↔ `i` mismatches (units 11, 14, 21, 28); (f) three speeches left without a closing quotation mark; (g) odd decompositions and unsupported asides in notes.

## Findings refused

- Unit 13 · i "their sin heavy" for ጽኑሕ (`l` "firm"): an English choice for the same adjective used of the judgment ("firm"); the sense overlaps, and the repetition would read badly. Left; flagged for pass 2 if it still looks odd.
- Unit 8 · n "Solomon's reproach": the Geʿez has no question particle and "you told me that they will perish" can be a statement or a challenge; the note's word is interpretive only. Left.
- Unit 26 · i "Then he said": ወይቤ opens a new sentence after ።; the house habit is to drop ወ- at sentence start (as in units 6, 9). Left.
- Unit 17 · i "as men" for ለሰብእ ("for man"): idiomatic, not a mistranslation. Left.
- Unit 12 · i "the righteous man" for ጻድቀ: the singular is correct for the accusative -ቀ and the note says it may be general; left.
- Unit 1 · n "forty-three … Matthew 1:17": the note states the text's count and the Gospel's groups without claiming they agree. Left.
- Unit 13 · ኢይሰሪ ("is not forgiven" vs "he does not forgive"): either is grammatical for ሰርየ (+ ሎሙ); the draft's passive is the more natural with ሎሙ; left.
- Unit 4 · "who was-carried" (እለ plural + 3fs ተጸውረት): the form is as in ch. 68a/b and the draft's note says the subject is ባሕርይ; left.
- Unit 24 · the identification of Jeroboam as Solomon's son (and "where Rehoboam would be expected"): consistent with ch. 36 and 67–68; no change.

## For pass 2 (gloss.json)

- ዜከረ/ዘከረ: ይዜክር (23) and ያዜክሩ (13) are from ዜከረ; any gloss entry must give ዜከረ, not ዘከረ.
- ትረስ: lemma ወረሰ (not ረሰየ); ትማእ: lemma uncertain (መውአ?) (?).
- ኢየኀድገክሙ: 3ms; ብቊዐኒ: በቊዐ imperative + -ኒ (the published ኢይበቊዕ entry can be broadened with it); ኅይስናሁ: ኅይስና (as in ch. 27/33–34), with the owner idiom; ተሀየየ: broaden/keep "turn away from (?)".
- The published known-forms entry for ፍኖቶሙ says "-ሆሙ, written -ቶሙ"; I believe the suffix is -ሙ after -ት (cf. ኀጢአቶሙ) and have written the note so. Not mine to change the published glossary; flagged.
- ባሕርይ "pearl", ሲኦል "Sheol", እግዚኣብሔር, መድኅን renderings checked against known-forms: consistent.
